what: Step 2: compare two periods and say how sure we are
title: Are hot days getting more common at Melbourne Airport?
text: summarise_periods() averages reliable years either side year choose, describe_periods() turns table sentences. “rough 95% range” gap two averages plus minus two standard errors. treats year independent, neighbouring hot years quite, read guide whether gap bigger ordinary year--year variation, formal test. nothing compare, function says instead reporting gap zero. , high threshold single month leaves hot days :
code: periods <- summarise_periods(ex, split_year = 2000) periods[, c("period", "n_years", "mean_exceed", "sd_exceed")] #>            period n_years mean_exceed sd_exceed #> 1 2000 or earlier      30      8.2000  4.693356 #> 2      after 2000      21     11.7619  5.009039 said <- describe_periods(periods, variable = "tmax", threshold = 35) said$headline #> [1] "In 2001–2021 the airport averaged 11.8 days a year with a daily maximum above 35 °C, against 8.2 in 1971–2000. That is 3.6 more hot days a year." said$how_sure #> [1] "The gap stands out from year-to-year noise: a rough 95% range for the difference is +0.8 to +6.3 days a year. This treats years as independent, so use it as a guide, not a formal test." rare <- annual_exceedances(threshold = 42, months = 7) describe_periods(summarise_periods(rare, split_year = 2000),                  variable = "tmax", threshold = 42)$headline #> [1] "No year in either period had a daily maximum above 42 °C."

what: Step 3: does the answer depend on the threshold?
title: Are hot days getting more common at Melbourne Airport?
text: conclusion holds 35 °C fragile. threshold_sensitivity() repeats comparison across range thresholds.  later period higher every threshold. gap days bigger low thresholds simply days. ratio column puts thresholds common footing: later years roughly 1.2 1.5 times many hot days thresholds, larger multiple rarest days, counts small noisier.
code: sens <- threshold_sensitivity(thresholds = c(30, 33, 35, 38, 40)) sens[, c("threshold", "mean_before", "mean_after", "difference")] #>   threshold mean_before mean_after difference #> 1        30  28.8333333  36.571429   7.738095 #> 2        33  14.2666667  20.190476   5.923810 #> 3        35   8.2000000  11.761905   3.561905 #> 4        38   3.0333333   4.571429   1.538095 #> 5        40   0.8333333   2.428571   1.595238 plot_sensitivity(threshold_sensitivity(), highlight = 35)
